summary: Worse than national despite the most 'progressive-governed' appearance: the wealthiest, most urbanised state wrapping the federal capital is not a safe harbour. In January 2026 the state government declared it 'will not allow LGBT promotion' and called for an investigation into a 'Glamping with Pride' gathering; in December 2025 the state's sultan used Friday sermons across state mosques to warn Muslims against LGBT practices — the monarchy-plus-religious-bureaucracy channel operating statewide. The state's religious department is the agency that pursued a well-known transgender entrepreneur with an arrest warrant and an all-out manhunt over her presentation, mobilising 122 religious affairs officers, which made this state the most visible arena for cross-dressing enforcement nationally. Countervailing: it also has the strongest documented prosecution record for violence against trans people — after a 32-year-old trans woman was beaten to death in Klang in 2018, four suspects were arrested and charged. Scored relative to the national score (0.16) for Malaysia.

Human Rights Watch dispatch (10 August 2022), 'State-Backed Discrimination Harms LGBT People in Malaysia': national analysis of religious authorities and state agencies driving anti-LGBT discrimination; documents the 2021 Nur Sajat case, in which this state's religious department issued an arrest warrant and mobilised 122 religious affairs officers to hunt her down over her attire, and her later flight from the country.

Human Rights Watch report (25 June 2019), "Deceased Can't Speak for Herself: Violence Against LGBT People in Malaysia": investigation of killings and violence against LGBT people in the country and the failures of investigation and justice in those cases, establishing the national violence-and-impunity pattern.

tangentialFactors: Anti-Pride hostility at the state level — the January 2026 probe into a 'Glamping with Pride' gathering and the official 'no LGBT promotion' stance — targets queer visibility generally and spills over onto trans visitors in the state's tourism corridor.
